title: OuiConfigFile
description: `oui.config.json` at the app's root: where the app keeps its routes, navigation and output, which design systems and mappings its controls come from, where its API is described, which of its pages are not yet bound, and which the assistant is never on. Paths are relative to the file. It is required and explicit: nothing an app depends on has a default, so a misconfigured app fails here, naming the setting, instead of generating an assistant that can do nothing. A setting the generator does not know is an error.

tsconfig.description: The tsconfig the app's source compiles with.

routes.description: The file whose routes decide where the app can go: `<Route>` elements (nested paths are joined to their parent, `index` routes kept, `React.lazy` followed) or a data router (`createBrowserRouter([...])`).

routeWrappers.description: Components a route's element is wrapped in that are never the page (`Suspense`, `ErrorBoundary`). Default none.

nav.description: Files holding the navigation entries (`{ label, route, group }` object literals). Default none.

designSystem.description: Design-system packages whose controls carry bindings (tier 1). Each must resolve from the app and name its control table in its `package.json` (`oui.agentControls`). `[]`: every control is tier 2 or in a room.

mappings.description: Tier 2 mappings (`tier2-mapping.json`), one per third-party design system the app does not own, by path. `oui generate` emits a bound module per mapping into `<out>/bound/` (named after the package: `@mantine/core` → `mantine-core.ts`, with its control table beside it), and reads every use of a bound control as it reads a tier 1 control. On an enforced page, importing a mapped control straight from its package is an error naming the bound import. A package is in `designSystem` or mapped, never both. Default none.

apiSpec.description: The API's OpenAPI 3 document, by module path, as the installed API client ships it (`@traidr/api-client/openapi.json`) — never a sibling checkout path, so the generator reads exactly the spec of the client version the app installs; or a path inside the app. Every `mutate` effect names one of its `operationId`s. `null`: the app declares no API, and a `mutate` effect is an error.

unbound.description: Page components whose interactive controls are not all bound yet. It may only get shorter: the generator fails for a listed page that is fully bound, so the list cannot rot. Every other page is enforced. Default none.

outside.description: Pages the assistant is never on: pages before sign-in, and public pages a link opens (a share link, a confirmation link). Each names its page by component or by route, with the reason. An outside page has no surface, its controls are not enforced, it is not among the pages the assistant goes to, and the knowledge says the assistant is not there. It is outside only if nothing around it or in it is the assistant's: no `shell` entry frames any of its routes; every element its routes render around it (a layout route's, or a `routeWrappers` component's, at any level) holds nothing someone can use and no person-only component; the page does not render the frame itself; and the page has no binding, display or room of its own (one a component shares with pages the assistant is on is that component's). A page listed here may not also be in `unbound`. Default none.

appCatalogs.description: Room catalogs the app itself declares (tier 3, a page's own editor), each loaded through the app's own Vite config so its modules resolve as the app build resolves them: the app needs `vite` among its own dependencies. Only their declarations are read. Default none.

shell.description: The app's frame: components mounted around the pages rather than by a route (a sidebar, a top bar, a phone tab bar, a toast host). Each becomes a `shell:` surface offered on the routes it frames, and its controls are enforced as a page's are, unless listed in `unbound`. Default none.

OutsideEntry.description: A page the assistant is never on: its page component, or one route it is on, and why. A page on several routes is outside on all of them: named by route, each of its routes is named.

component.description: The page component, as the routes name it.

reason.description: Why the assistant is never there ("before sign-in", "a public share link").

route.description: A route pattern, exactly as the routes give it (`/watch/:clipId`).

reason.description: Why the assistant is never there ("before sign-in", "a public share link").

ShellEntry.description: One part of the app's frame.

module.description: The module, relative to the app root.

export.description: The export that is the frame's component.

routes.description: The route patterns it frames. Default every route (`*`).

AppCatalogEntry.description: A room catalog the app declares.

module.description: The module, relative to the app root.

export.description: The export that is the catalog.

hosts.description: App components whose use puts the room on a page.
